study.title: Electroacupuncture rewires interhemispheric homotopic connectivity to promote motor recovery after ischemic stroke
study.study_design: Randomized controlled animal experiment (rat model); three-group parallel design with pre-post intervention resting-state fMRI
study.randomization: Rats were randomly assigned to three groups
study.blinding: Neurological deficit scores assessed by an observer blinded to the experimental groups
study.population: Twenty-four clean-grade female Sprague-Dawley rats (weight: 250-280 g)
study.disease_condition: Ischemic stroke (transient focal cerebral ischemia via middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion, MCAO/R model)
study.inclusion_criteria: Clean-grade female Sprague-Dawley rats, weight 250-280 g
study.exclusion_criteria: Animals exhibiting severe distress or significant weight loss (>20% baseline body weight) meeting predefined humane endpoints were euthanized

conditions.scan_context: Resting-state fMRI acquired before intervention period

conditions.timepoint_exact: Day 11 (24 h after the final EA session)
conditions.scan_context: Resting-state fMRI acquired 24 h after final EA session; under dexmedetomidine + 1.5% isoflurane anesthesia

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: GV20 (Baihui); one electrode at GV20, other electrode attached to tail
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.25 mm in diameter, 13 mm in length
interventions.manipulation_exact: needle placed at GV20, connected to one electrode of an SDZ-II EA stimulator; the other electrode was attached to the tail to complete the circuit
interventions.electrical_intensity_exact: 2 mA (producing visible twitching of the limb musculature)
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Numerous preclinical studies have demonstrated that EA at GV20 can improve neurobehavioral outcomes of rodent stroke models, reduce infarct volume, and promote neurogenesis and angiogenesis

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Same anesthesia treatment but no acupuncture or EA
Same anesthesia treatment but no acupuncture or EA; sham surgery without filament insertion

extraction_notes.note: Exact numerical values for Mnss scores at each timepoint (Day 1, Day 3, Day 7) are not reported in the text and are only depicted in Figure 4A as bar graphs; they could not be reliably extracted from the figure.

The paper reports MNI coordinates but this is a rat fMRI study. The use of 'MNI coordinates' for a rodent brain atlas is unusual; the coordinate space label may refer to a rat-specific atlas registered in MNI-like space or a rat brain atlas. This should be interpreted with caution. The paper does not specify the rat brain atlas used for normalization.

In Table 3, the region 'R_Hippocampus_Postero_Dorsal' has an x-coordinate of -0.83923 (negative), which would normally suggest the left hemisphere. The label says 'R_' (Right). This may be a labeling error in the paper. Extracted as reported.
Cluster extent unit is not explicitly stated in the tables. Units are assumed to be voxels but this is not confirmed in the methods.
Sensory/deqi responses are not measured or reported; this is an animal study and no subjective sensation data can be collected.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding assessments are not applicable to an animal study and were not reported.

The paper does not report the pre-intervention (baseline) VMHC comparisons between groups (sham vs. model, sham vs. EA), only longitudinal changes in the model group and post-intervention comparisons.

The paper describes EA treatment as '1-week treatment (5 days)' but the abstract states '1-week treatment.' The number of sessions is explicitly stated as 5 days (5 sessions) in the methods; extracted as 5 sessions.

The abstract states 'EA significantly increased VMHC in subcortical motor regions (p = 0.001, alphasim correction)' but the tables do not report a p=0.001 threshold directly associated with EA vs. model; the main ANOVA F=8.18, p<0.001. The p=0.001 cited in the abstract appears to refer to the voxel-wise threshold used in the whole-brain analysis.

The paper states that rs-fMRI was acquired on day 11 as the post-intervention timepoint, but does not explicitly state when the pre-intervention scan was acquired. The pre-intervention scan timing is inferred from the experimental flowchart.

The paper's abstract states r2=0.206, p=0.009 for the IC-Mnss correlation. In the Results section (3.4), it states 'R2 = 0.206, p = 0.009' for ic and 'R2 = 0.374, p = 0.0002' for globus pallidus. The figure caption confirms these. Both were extracted as reported.
No histological validation was performed; authors acknowledge this as a limitation.

The Generative AI statement discloses that AI was used for 'Polishing article with AI.' This may affect the precision of language in the methods/results sections and could introduce ambiguity in interpretation.
The normalization template (rat brain atlas) used for spatial normalization is not explicitly named in the methods. Only SPM12 and REST toolkit are mentioned.
